speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of fear and worry about the future with AI.
zh: 对于 AI 的未来，存在很多恐惧和担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about this idea that if you fall behind, you're going to become part of this permanent underclass.
zh: 我想谈谈这个观点：如果你落后了，你就会成为这个永久下层阶级的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a funny, dark fantasy that we seem to have as Silicon Valley collectively.
zh: 这是我们硅谷集体似乎都有的一种有趣的、黑暗的幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like things have never been better by almost every measure.
zh: 尽管几乎从任何指标来看，情况都从未如此之好。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a technology that really amplifies our agency.
zh: 这是一项真正放大我们主观能动性的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It kind of unbundles skill from desire.
zh: 它在某种程度上把技能从欲望中拆分出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not only can we dramatically drive productivity, we can dramatically drive ambition.
zh: 我们不仅能大幅提升生产力，还能大幅提升雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you get too ambitious?
zh: 雄心会不会太大？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there like a limit?
zh: 有没有一种限制？

speaker: Unknown
en: In the old days, three years ago, we would see a company and if what they were trying to do was too ambitious, we would not engage.
zh: 在过去，三年前，我们会看到一家公司，如果他们想做的事情太雄心勃勃，我们就不会接触。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, we're almost seeing the opposite problem.
zh: 今天，我们几乎看到了相反的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: An idea that's too small is not something that we want to engage with.
zh: 一个太小的想法不是我们想接触的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you have this interesting take that company building more and more is going to become this kind of series of creating loops?
zh: 你有一个有趣的观点：公司建设越来越会成为一种创建循环的过程？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're going to see this sort of cascading set of everything from a loop per person to loops that can run large parts of the company.
zh: 我认为我们会看到这种级联的情况，从每人一个循环到能运营公司大部分业务的循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: With that said, I think humans are a critical ingredient.
zh: 话虽如此，我认为人类是一个关键要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: The loop will help you climb to the local maxima, but then it plateaus.
zh: 循环会帮助你爬到局部最大值，但随后它会进入平台期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need human intuition.
zh: 你需要人类的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need somebody to actually help you land at the base of the next hill.
zh: 你需要有人真正帮助你降落在下一座山的山脚。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have this take that the big opportunity is this idea of, Luke, make me happier.
zh: 我们有一个观点：最大的机会就是这个想法，Luke,让我更快乐。

speaker: Unknown
en: We believe that people want to be more productive, but they don't.
zh: 我们相信人们想要更高效，但其实并不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think more people want to spend time than save time.
zh: 我觉得更多的人想要花时间而不是节省时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that the opportunity for this technology is the basics of consumer need.
zh: 所以我认为这项技术的机会在于消费者需求的基本面。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we feel more connected, more loved?
zh: 我们如何感受到更多连接、更多被爱？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we make progress?
zh: 我们如何取得进步？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we have fun?
zh: 我们如何获得乐趣？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think it's a model or a capability challenge.
zh: 我不认为这是一个模型或能力上的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a product design challenge.
zh: 这只是一个产品设计上的挑战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today's episode comes from our recommended listening series where we feature standout conversations from people across our broader network.
zh: 今天这一期来自我们的推荐收听系列，我们会呈现来自我们更广泛网络中杰出人物的精彩对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: This one comes from Lenny's podcast, where Lenny Richitsky sits down with A16Z general partner Anish Acharya for a wide-ranging conversation about AI, company building, and why Anish thinks we should be more ambitious about what this technology makes possible.
zh: 这一期来自 Lenny 的播客，Lenny Richitsky 与 A16Z 普通合伙人 Anish Acharya 展开了一场广泛的对话，涉及 AI、公司建设，以及为什么 Anish 认为我们应该对这项技术所带来的可能性抱有更大的雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: They get into Anish's idea that companies are becoming a series of loops, with AI increasingly handling repeatable work, while humans step in with judgment, intuition, and new ideas.
zh: 他们深入探讨了 Anish 的观点：公司正在变成一系列的循环，AI 越来越多地处理可重复的工作，而人类则以判断力、直觉和新想法介入。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also discuss why he's skeptical of fears around an AI permanent underclass, where the biggest opportunities in consumer AI may emerge, and why moats are often discovered rather than designed.
zh: 他们还讨论了为什么他对 AI 永久下层阶级的恐惧持怀疑态度、消费级 AI 的最大机会可能出现在哪里，以及为什么护城河往往是被发现而不是被设计出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And his advice for navigating all of this is pretty simple.
zh: 他对如何应对这一切的建议非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Build something.
zh: 去构建一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fastest way to understand where AI is going is to use the models, ship things, and develop your own intuition.
zh: 理解 AI 走向的最快方式就是去使用这些模型、发布东西，并培养你自己的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, my guest is Anish Acharya.
zh: 今天我的嘉宾是 Anish Acharya。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anish is general partner at A16Z, where he focuses on consumer investing.
zh: Anish 是 A16Z 的普通合伙人，专注于消费领域投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: He is one of the most insightful, thought-provoking, mind-expanding, in the weeds product investors I've met.
zh: 他是我见过的最有洞察力、最发人深省、最能拓展思维、最深入产品细节的投资人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's been at A16Z for over seven years now.
zh: 他已经在 A16Z 工作了七年多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And unlike a lot of VCs, and why I loved having Anish on the podcast is that he is a longtime product builder and founder.
zh: 与很多 VC 不同——这也是我喜欢请 Anish 来播客的原因——他是一位长期的产品构建者和创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: He founded a company called Social Deck, which he sold to Google and then ended up leading a number of efforts within Google.
zh: 他创立了一家名为 Social Deck 的公司，卖给了 Google，之后在 Google 内部领导了多个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then he started a new company called Snowball, which he then again sold, this time to Credit Karma, where he moved to VPR product and then GM of the broader consumer product and the whole entire credit card business.
zh: 然后他创办了一家名为 Snowball 的新公司，之后又再次卖掉，这次卖给了 Credit Karma，在那里他担任产品 VP，随后担任更广泛的消费产品以及整个信用卡业务的 GM。

speaker: Unknown
en: This conversation will get your mind buzzing.
zh: 这场对话会让你的思维活跃起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anish, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
zh: Anish，非常感谢你能来到这里，欢迎来到播客。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you, Lenny.
zh: 谢谢你，Lenny。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm so excited to be here, thrilled.
zh: 我非常兴奋能来到这里，非常激动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to start with a very light topic.
zh: 我想从一个非常轻松的话题开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to talk about this meme of the permanent underclass.
zh: 我想谈谈永久下层阶级这个梗。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's kind of this joke that people half joke about, this idea that if you kind of fall behind and aren't just like on top of all the latest AI tools, aren't becoming the most productive person ever, you're going to become part of this permanent underclass and fall behind and have a really hard time.
zh: 这是人们半开玩笑地说的一个笑话，意思是如果你落后了，没有掌握所有最新的 AI 工具，没有成为有史以来最高效的人，你就会成为这个永久下层阶级的一员，落后于人，过得很艰难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And some people joke about it.
zh: 有些人拿它开玩笑。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of people take this really seriously and stresses a lot of people out.
zh: 我觉得很多人非常认真地对待这件事，这让很多人感到压力很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: How real of a concern do you think this really is?
zh: 你觉得这个问题实际有多严重？

speaker: Unknown
en: How seriously do you think people should take this?
zh: 你认为人们应该多认真地对待这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not very seriously.
zh: 不用太认真。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's a funny, dark fantasy that we seem to have as, you know, Silicon Valley collectively.
zh: 而且这是我们作为，你知道，整个硅谷集体似乎共有的一种有趣的、黑暗的幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like things have never been better, really by almost every measure, by how sort of distributed all the opportunities are, by the kind of technology we have access to, to the types of ambition we're allowed to have.
zh: 比如，几乎按任何标准衡量，事情从未像现在这么好，无论是机会的分散程度，还是我们能接触到的技术种类，以及我们被允许拥有的抱负类型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to the number of companies that are sort of independently working on things that are winning.
zh: 还有那些在各自领域独立做事并且正在获胜的公司数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet there's this sort of discussion of permanent underclass, being outside of the light cone, I've heard it.
zh: 然而却有这样一种关于“永久底层阶级”、“处于光锥之外”的讨论，我听说过这种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not just something for deep insiders or outsiders.
zh: 而且这不仅仅是深层内部人士或局外人的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like there's a real fear kind of from, you know, researchers at foundation model labs all the way through to the Silicon Valley laymen.
zh: 感觉从基础模型实验室的研究人员一直到硅谷的普通从业者，都存在一种真实的恐惧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, here's like a couple of points that I think are really important.
zh: 我是说，这里有几个我认为非常重要的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So first, I think the last era of tech was a lot more centralized.
zh: 首先，我认为上一个科技时代的中心化程度要高得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at network effects, that's sort of the gold standard.
zh: 如果你看网络效应，那算是黄金标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: You worked on a network effects product.
zh: 你做网络效应产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the gold standard of businesses from the mobile era.
zh: 那是移动时代商业模式的黄金标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those things led to dramatic centralization, right?
zh: 而这些东西导致了戏剧性的中心化，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, all of them are definitionally sort of end of one networks.
zh: 当然，它们从定义上讲都是“一家独大”的网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at what's happening now, it's like every part of the stack, there's not even two relevant players, there's like 20.
zh: 如果你看看现在正在发生的事，就是技术栈的每一层，都不止两个相关玩家，而是有大约 20 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you've got labs, you've got open weight, you've got different variations within both.
zh: 你知道，你有实验室，你有开放权重，两者内部还有不同的变体。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at coding agents, we were talking about it, like your mental model for two years ago should have been, would have been, I think it should be winner take all.
zh: 如果你看编程智能体，我们之前聊过，两年前你的心智模型应该是，我认为应该会是赢家通吃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet Claude Code, Codex, lovable.
zh: 然而却是 Claude Code、Codex、lovable。

speaker: Unknown
en: Replit, Wabi, like they're all sort of working.
zh: Replit、Wabi，它们都在某种程度上运转良好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's really, really encouraging to see that.
zh: 所以看到这一点真的非常非常令人鼓舞。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the second thing, you've heard all the kind of economic data, everything from radiologists who are supposed to be cooked every year for, I think, about 20 years now.
zh: 你知道，第二件事，你已经听过各种经济数据了，从放射科医生说起——我认为大约 20 年来，每年都有人说他们要完蛋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, job postings are higher than they've ever been, as well as programmers, you know?
zh: 而当然，职位招聘数量比以往任何时候都高，程序员也一样，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't know that the empirical data bears it out.
zh: 所以我不认为经验数据支持那种说法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the final thing is that...
zh: 我认为最后一点是……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this sort of discussion about RSI.
zh: 关于 RSI 有这样一种讨论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know RSI is like recursive self-improvement is a fun term to throw around.
zh: 我知道 RSI 就是递归自我改进，是个很好拿来炫的术语。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you ask the most sophisticated individuals at the labs, it's not actually RSI that's occurring, which could lead to some sort of runaway winner because they were an epsilon ahead of the others.
zh: 但如果你问实验室里最有见识的那些人，实际发生的并不是 RSI——那种情况可能因为某家比别家领先一个 epsilon 而导致某种失控的赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's auto catalytic effects, which just means you're using the new technology to improve your process, but it's not truly recursive.
zh: 发生的是自催化效应，意思只是你在用新技术改进自己的流程，但它并不是真正递归的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So
zh: 所以

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everything from the most empirical to the most technical view points in the other direction.
zh: 我认为从最经验性的到最技术性的视角，一切都指向另一个方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yet we can't seem to let go of this fantasy.
zh: 然而我们似乎就是放不下这个幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something I've been thinking about recently is seeing all these, like even seeing these crazy stories about OpenAI's models, hacking, hugging face.
zh: 我最近在思考的一件事是，看到所有这些，比如看到关于 OpenAI 的模型入侵 Hugging Face 的那些疯狂报道。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these stories to me feels like there's always been this question of are we on the fast takeoff or the slow takeoff scenario?
zh: 所有这些报道让我感觉，一直存在这样一个问题：我们处在快速起飞还是缓慢起飞的情景中？

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels very much so that we are on the slow takeoff scenario.
zh: 而感觉非常明确的是，我们处在缓慢起飞的情景中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because every one of these milestones is like, holy shit, it hacked.
zh: 因为每一个这样的里程碑都像是，我靠，它入侵了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We had no idea it was doing this.
zh: 我们完全不知道它在做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like we're catching it, we're watching it, we're observing it, we're iterating, evolving.
zh: 但就像，我们正在抓住它，我们在看着它，我们在观察它，我们在迭代、演进。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's always this fear, okay, but tomorrow it's going to take off.
zh: 总是有这种恐惧：好吧，但明天它就要起飞了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I'm hearing from you is that's probably not the case, which I think is the source of a lot of people's fear is this idea that all of a sudden it's going to become super, super intelligent and then we're in big trouble.
zh: 我从你这里听到的是，情况可能并非如此，而我认为这正是很多人恐惧的来源，即这种想法：它会突然变得超级超级智能，然后我们就麻烦大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the line of reasoning for that case is always everything up until now, then something happens that no one can quite articulate and then fast take off.
zh: 因为那种论点的推理链条永远是：到目前为止的一切，然后发生了某种没人能说清楚的事，然后就快速起飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't believe that that's going to happen.
zh: 所以我不相信那会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think that model progress is happening faster than ever before.
zh: 我确实认为模型进展正以空前的速度发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you look at something like economic diffusion, you know, I grew up in a small town, I went back home last summer, like people's lives haven't changed that much.
zh: 但如果你看经济扩散之类的东西，你知道，我在一个小镇长大，去年夏天我回了趟老家，人们的生活并没有太大变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if nothing else, the sort of slow rate of economic diffusion will catch it.
zh: 所以退一万步说，经济扩散的缓慢速度也会把它兜住。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the other thing that's under-discussed, Lenny, is how many problems are truly intelligence-bound?
zh: 我认为另一件被讨论得不够的事，Lenny，是有多少问题真正受制于智能？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you had a data center of PhDs working at FedEx or Domino's Pizza, are they going to be exponentially dominating supply chain and pizzas?
zh: 如果你有一个由博士生组成的数据中心，在 FedEx 或达美乐披萨工作，他们能在供应链和披萨上呈指数级地称霸吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我不这么认为。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we might be overestimating how many problems are intelligence-bound versus bound by other things.
zh: 所以我觉得我们可能高估了多少问题是受智能限制的，而不是受其他因素限制的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you seeing inside of companies in terms of, is there more of a divide happening?
zh: 你在公司内部看到了什么？是不是出现了更多的分化？

speaker: Unknown
en: And do you think there will be more of a divide between the people that are becoming really good and embracing versus like, I don't have time for this.
zh: 你觉得在真正变得很强、积极拥抱的人和那些说“我没时间搞这个”的人之间，会出现更大的分化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I hate all this stuff.
zh: 我讨厌所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: My job's already so stressful.
zh: 我的工作已经压力够大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you seeing happening?
zh: 你看到了什么在发生？

speaker: Unknown
en: And where do you think things will go inside of companies in terms of maybe a divide?
zh: 你觉得在公司内部，就可能的分化而言，事情会走向哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I have so many thoughts on this.
zh: 我的意思是，对此我有很多想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think we give the average employee enough credit.
zh: 我觉得我们没有给普通员工足够的信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we have this abstraction of a white-collar employee.
zh: 我们有一种关于白领员工的抽象概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the white-collar manager, the abstraction is like some Dilbert-esque manager who's just shuffling paper all day long.
zh: 你知道的，白领经理，这个抽象概念就像某个整天只是推着文件转的 Dilbert 式经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we have this abstraction of consumers that they're sort of these low-agency NBCs.
zh: 你知道的，我们对消费者也有一种抽象概念，认为他们是某种低主观能动性的 NBC。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course, that would never apply to us or our friends.
zh: 当然，那永远不会适用于我们或我们的朋友。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we have this abstraction that everybody else's job is super automatable by AI, but of course ours is not.
zh: 你知道的，我们有一种抽象概念，认为其他所有人的工作都超级容易被 AI 自动化，但当然我们自己的不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think when you actually get into the details, a lot of people are actually excited to, you know, better themselves, get more leverage.
zh: 所以我觉得当你真正深入细节时，很多人其实很兴奋去提升自己、获得更多杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you see this with, of course, sophisticated companies like Google, but even a company like Kavak.
zh: 你当然能在 Google 这样成熟的公司看到这一点，但甚至像 Kavak 这样的公司也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: where they sell, you know, used cars in Mexico.
zh: 他们在墨西哥卖二手车。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've got this concept of a Jedi Academy where they're teaching everybody at the company, including the mechanics, how to use the new tools and technologies.
zh: 他们有一个叫 Jedi Academy 的概念，在公司里教每一个人，包括机械师，如何使用新的工具和技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of at the end of the six week course, they ship a cutting edge in production agent.
zh: 在六周课程结束时，他们会上线一个尖端的、在生产环境运行的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually think that more people are embracing the technology than we sort of like to discuss.
zh: 所以我实际上认为，拥抱这项技术的人比我们喜欢讨论的要多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big change is going to be using AI versus reorganizing your entire company around AI.
zh: 重大变化将是使用 AI，而不是围绕 AI 重组你的整个公司。

zh: 结果发现那恰恰是 AI 最擅长的：那些可验证的、你知道成功长什么样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question I think about now is just like, which skills can you not just turn into a loop because the output is so hard to verify?
zh: 所以我现在思考的问题就是：哪些技能是你没法直接变成一个循环的，因为输出太难验证？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think that's right.
zh: 是的，我觉得你说得对。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that those are going to be the rate limiting factors because you can only do one steak dinner a night.
zh: 而且我认为那些会成为限速因素，因为你一晚上只能吃一顿牛排晚餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess you could do a steak lunch.
zh: 我猜你可以再来一顿牛排午餐。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, to some extent, there's going to be these rate limiting factors in every system.
zh: 但是，你知道的，在某种程度上，每个系统里都会有这些限速因素。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a useful way to think about it is anytime the model's making a mistake or doing something you wouldn't do, what do you know that it doesn't know?
zh: 我认为一个有用的思考方式是：每当模型犯了错或做了你不会做的事，问问自己，你知道什么是它不知道的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a really interesting example I heard from Ale at Kavak.
zh: 我从 Kavak 的 Ale 那里听到一个非常有趣的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's probably the most sophisticated thinker on this stuff that I get to hang out with, where he said anytime they have an agent per customer, they sell used cars online, and when the agent gets stuck, it actually calls a human.
zh: 他可能是我能一起交流的人当中在这类问题上思考最深入的一位，他说每当他们有一个面向每个客户的智能体时——他们在网上卖二手车——当智能体卡住了，它实际上会打给一个人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the human will coach the agent through.
zh: 然后这个人类会引导智能体走出困境。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now the magic of that is not only does it unblock the agent, but of course the agent then captures all the traces and learns from it.
zh: 这里的妙处在于，它不仅解除了智能体的阻塞，而且当然，智能体会随后捕捉所有轨迹并从中学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that's a really interesting mental model.
zh: 这是一个非常有趣的思维模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's either a knowledge gap or a data gap that you have to give the agent.
zh: 它要么是知识缺口，要么是数据缺口，需要你补给智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the next time it shouldn't have to call you.
zh: 这样下一次它就不必再打给你了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that example.
zh: 我喜欢这个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Basically the takeaway here is...
zh: 基本上这里的要点是……

en: You need to start thinking about every function as an agent loop.
zh: 你需要开始把每一个职能都当作一个智能体循环来思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the job is to figure out where it gets blocked, where it goes wrong, and give it more context, more insight, more direction, basically.
zh: 你的工作是找出它在哪里被卡住、在哪里出错，然后给它更多上下文、更多洞见、更多方向，基本上是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then hopefully a lot of your day-to-day work, you know, when you come up with a new idea that works, the kind of implications of that idea, if it's a product, you know, there's marketing work, there's sales work, there's product marketing, there's communication, there's legal, all of that should be largely handled for you.
zh: 然后希望你的很多日常工作，你知道，当你想出一个有效的新点子时，这个点子带来的各种影响，如果它是一个产品，你知道，会有营销工作、销售工作、产品营销、传播、法务，所有这些应该很大程度上都替你处理好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And your idea, you know, your job is to go take a hike and dream the dreams and come up with the next hill to climb.
zh: 而你的点子，你知道，你的工作就是去远足、做梦，想出下一座要攀登的山峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this begs the question a bit of just what will separate the companies that win in this world where AI is kind of doing a lot of this?
zh: 这就引出了一个问题：在这个 AI 包揽了很多这类工作的世界里，什么会区分出赢家公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: I imagine part of the answer is the human in this local maxima coming in with a better idea.
zh: 我猜想答案的一部分是处在这种局部最优中的人带着更好的点子进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else that you think becomes like a differentiator in this world where AI is doing so much of the work that humans are currently doing?
zh: 在这个 AI 承担了这么多目前由人类完成的工作的世界里，你认为还有其他什么会成为差异化因素吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think one thing that's under discussed is that it's unclear that the sort of competitive equilibria that exists in a lot of industries will really change.
zh: 我是说，我认为有一个被讨论得不够的点是：很多行业中现存的那种竞争均衡是否会真的改变，这一点并不清楚。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, so let's say Pizza Hut and Domino's and Papa John's and Roundtable all get a data center of PhDs.
zh: 你知道，比如说 Pizza Hut、Domino's、Papa John's 和 Roundtable 都得到了一个由博士组成的数据中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, they're all going to either adopt it or have a CEO change and adopt it.
zh: 而且，你知道，它们都会要么采用它，要么换一个 CEO 然后采用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it'll be a rocky period and there'll be some, you know, relative shuffling.
zh: 所以会有一段颠簸期，也会有一些，你知道，相对的洗牌。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that they're all going to embrace the new technology because most companies do.
zh: 但我认为它们都会拥抱新技术，因为大多数公司都会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know that one of them is going to have 99% of the market.
zh: 我不认为其中某一家会占有 99% 的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think kind of what's under discussed is that, yes, in the near term, I think there'll be winners and losers based on adoption of the technology and kind of how ambitiously you adopt it.
zh: 所以我认为被讨论得不够的一点是：是的，在短期内，我认为会有基于技术采用情况的赢家和输家，以及你采用得多有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I do think there's a lot of industries that will sort of maintain their current competitive dynamics because they're not intelligence bound.
zh: 但我确实认为有很多行业会大体维持它们当前的竞争格局，因为它们不受智能约束。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the most useful question to ask yourself as a founder CEO is just, hey, if we assume these things are infinitely intelligent and astonishingly cheap, how would we reorganize the company?
zh: 我认为作为一个创始人 CEO,问自己最有用的问题就是：嘿，如果我们假设这些东西拥有无限的智能而且便宜得惊人，我们会如何重组这家公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's where we're going.
zh: 因为我们正朝着那个方向走。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of along those lines, you have this interesting take about this kind of split that might be coming within companies between these generalists and specialists and how AI plays into that.
zh: 沿着这个思路，你有一个有趣的观点，是关于公司内部可能出现的通才与专才之间的分裂，以及 AI 如何在其中发挥作用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about that.
zh: 谈谈这个吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, I think that there's so many interesting things that this touches on.
zh: 是的，我认为这件事牵扯到太多有趣的东西了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, one is the question of open weight versus frontier.
zh: 你知道，其中之一是开放权重与前沿模型的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm sure, are you familiar with kind of Pareto efficiency?
zh: 那么，我敢说，你熟悉帕累托效率这类概念吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure you are.
zh: 你肯定熟悉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Please explain.
zh: 请解释一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so Pareto efficiency is just, you know, for price performance, for example, what is the kind of, the efficient frontier is what's considered the optimal trade-off of, you know, a unit of performance for a unit of price.
zh: 是的，帕累托效率就是，你知道，以性价比为例，所谓的有效前沿被认为是用一单位价格换取一单位性能的最优权衡。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, are you sort of, if you're along that curve, you're always paying the rational amount for the performance.
zh: 而且，你知道，如果你处在那条曲线上，你为性能付出的总是理性的价格。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's interesting is that frontier models are actually irrationally priced in that, you know, first of all, Mythos is infinite dollars a token, you can't use it.
zh: 有趣的是，前沿模型实际上定价是不理性的，你知道，首先，Mythos 是每 token 无限美元，你根本用不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you look at even something like Fable 5, you know, for one IQ, conceptually one IQ of extra intelligence, you're paying 100x more.
zh: 但即便看 Fable 5 这样的东西，你知道，为了概念上一 IQ 的额外智能，你要多付 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not rational, but I think there's a lot of jobs in which you have unbounded upside, like drug discovery, you know?
zh: 所以这不理性，但我认为有很多工作的上行空间是无界的，比如药物研发，你知道？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if that one IQ point lets you discover the next, you know, statin, it's a trillion dollar outcome.
zh: 如果那一 IQ 点让你发现了下一个，你知道，他汀类药物，那就是万亿美元级别的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's sort of rational to pay for the highest intelligence in these types of jobs and industries.
zh: 所以在这类工作和行业中，为最高智能付费是理性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, on the other hand, I'm going to pick on, you know, maybe legal.
zh: 而另一方面，我要拿，你知道，也许是法务来开刀。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's perhaps only so much upside to be had in legal or finance.
zh: 在法务或金融领域，可能上行空间就只有那么多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for those jobs, you actually do want to be very Pareto efficient and probably pay for, you know, good performance at a good price, not infinitely priced, infinite potential upside performance.
zh: 对于那些工作，你实际上确实想要非常帕累托高效，很可能为，你知道，好价格下的好性能付费，而不是为无限定价、有无限潜在上行空间的性能付费。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think what we're going to see is a split between job functions that demand kind of mid IQ intelligence.
zh: 所以我认为我们将看到的是：需要中等 IQ 级别智能的职能会出现分化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those will often be open weight, sort of biased with reinforcement learning, you know, things that make the models even cheaper, more performant for a narrow job, along with, you know, incredibly, quote unquote, expensive, but performant frontier tokens.
zh: 那些往往会是开放权重的、用强化学习做偏好调优的，你知道，那些让模型在狭窄工作中更便宜、更高性能的东西，与之并存的还有，你知道，极其——所谓——「昂贵」但高性能的前沿 token。

speaker: Unknown
en: For sales, support, research, engineering.
zh: 用于销售、支持、研究、工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think you're going to end up having both architectures and, you know, we can touch on this in a little bit, but I do think there are these sort of comparative advantages amongst model families and then also amongst, of course, individual models that we're seeing more and more of.
zh: 所以我认为你最终会同时拥有两种架构，而且，你知道，我们稍后可以再谈这个，但我确实认为在这些模型家族之间存在着某种比较优势，当然，在单个模型之间也越来越多地是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not going to be one or the other.
zh: 不会是非此即彼的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Such an interesting insight.
zh: 这个洞察真有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just to make sure I understand what you're describing here, you're thinking there's going to be this split between kind of within an org.
zh: 所以为了确保我理解你在这里描述的内容，你的想法是在一个组织内部会有这样的分化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Function and model where specific functions that have a lot more upside and in potential leverage go for the frontier models.
zh: 职能和模型之间，那些上升空间更大、潜在杠杆更大的特定职能会用前沿模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you describe these kind of product sales, engineering, research roles.
zh: 你说的这类是产品、销售、工程、研究角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's like, and then for other functions, you don't need, you don't need mythos.
zh: 然后就是，对于其他职能，你不需要，你不需要 mythos。

zh: 你不需要 Astra，我记得那是最新的那个？

zh: 对对对。

zh: 所以你的意思是，AI 不需要是前沿模型，人也不必是世界上最聪明的人，在那个世界里也能做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 对，我不想显得贬低。

zh: 那些职位职能里有非常出色的人。

zh: 我只是认为他们所处理的问题是上升空间有限的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you can only kind of close the books correctly.
zh: 那种感觉是，天哪，我能做到这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, you can't close the books 100x better.
zh: 你没法把账做得好 100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, that's exactly what I'm saying.
zh: 所以对，我说的就是这个意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wonder if it's connected back to that discussion we had earlier about it's verifiable.
zh: 我在想这是不是和我们之前那次讨论有关联，就是关于它是可验证的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's a lot more verifiable, you don't need the frontier model versus, I don't know, the potential upside.
zh: 如果它更可验证，你就不需要前沿模型，不像那种，我不知道，潜在上升空间大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure.
zh: 我不确定。

zh: 我认为真正的问题是有多少上升空间，以及计算它有多难？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, here's a nuance.
zh: 比如，这里有个细微之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: Customer support, a customer may call in and report a bug.
zh: 客户支持，一个客户可能会打进来报告一个 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: That bug may actually be the first breadcrumb to a thing that changes our entire organization.
zh: 那个 bug 可能实际上是能改变我们整个组织的事情的第一条线索。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if the CEO was on that call or the smartest person, they could follow the trail.
zh: 如果 CEO 在那个电话上，或者是最聪明的人在，他们就能顺藤摸瓜。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if we actually have this, quote unquote, mid IQ generalist, then not.
zh: 但如果我们实际用的是这个所谓的「中等智商的通才」，那就不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: That actually makes the case for as a basket of problems always use frontier intelligence.
zh: 这实际上构成了这样一个论点：作为一个问题集合，应该总是使用前沿智能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can, of course, make the case for the mid IQ basket as well, which is simply that we've crossed an intelligence threshold for almost every economically useful problem.
zh: 当然，我也能为中等智商集合辩护，理由很简单：对于几乎每一个经济上有用的问题，我们都已经跨过了智能门槛。

speaker: Unknown
en: And anything beyond that threshold is simply waste.
zh: 超过那个门槛的任何东西都只是浪费。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而且，我觉得，人们忘记的一点是，那些非前沿模型，它们就是，那大概就是六个月前的前沿水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were so impressed and we loved it.
zh: 我们当时那么惊艳，我们那么喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like, holy shit, I can do all this.

zh: 每个模型各擅长什么？

en: Yes.

zh: 你知道，如你所知，每位侍酒师的秘诀是一万个小时，或者可能是一万瓶酒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that the secret of being a model sommelier is just using them all.
zh: 所以我认为成为模型侍酒师的秘诀就是把它们全都用一遍。

en: And I think you learn so much.
zh: 我觉得你会学到非常多。

en: You know, I think for people who believe the models are commodities or totally fungible, you just haven't actually used the models.
zh: 你知道，我认为那些相信模型是大宗商品或完全可互换的人，只是实际上没有用过这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many of the kind of, you know, the Ev Williams, the Kevin Roses, that's who they were painters, except technology was their canvas.
zh: 很多那种,你知道,Ev Williams、Kevin Rose 那样的人,他们就是画家,只不过技术是他们的画布。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they created this very funny product called Card Versus Card where they shipped I think 100,000 people a debit card and then every day they would text those people with a location that they had to spend the money at and they would put $100 on the card and everyone would rush out to spend the money and one or two would be able to spend it and everybody else would get declined.
zh: 所以他们做了这个非常有趣的产品叫 Card Versus Card,他们给大概 10 万人寄了借记卡,然后每天他们会给这些人发短信,告知一个地点,他们必须在那里把钱花掉,他们会在卡里放 100 美元,所有人都会冲出去花钱,只有一两个人能花掉,其他所有人都会被拒付。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was just this hilarious social experiment that went hyper-viral.
zh: 这就是一个特别爆笑的社交实验,超级病毒式传播。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for me, it was always inspiring in the world of fintech because it was like, wow, why don't we build more products like that?
zh: 对我来说,在金融科技的世界里它一直很鼓舞人心,因为就像,哇,我们为什么不多做一些那样的产品呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, money is inherently social and yet all the financial products we have are so dry and personal and embarrassing.
zh: 你知道,钱本质上是社交性的,然而我们所有的金融产品都那么枯燥、私密、令人尴尬。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a sort of similar moment happening in AI right now where we can build these wildly ambitious products that touch on many of our social nerves.
zh: 我觉得 AI 领域现在正发生着一个类似的时刻,我们可以构建这些极其宏大的产品,触及我们许多社交神经。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just have to do it.
zh: 我们只需要去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me follow that thread.
zh: 那让我顺着这个话题往下说。

speaker: Unknown
en: You get to see tons of companies both pitching you and also companies you're working with that you're investing in.
zh: 你能看到大量的公司,既有向你路演的,也有你正在合作并且投资的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some counterintuitive lessons you've learned from watching the companies that operate well and have succeeded?
zh: 从观察那些运营良好并取得成功的公司中,你学到了哪些反直觉的经验?

speaker: Unknown
en: Lessons that maybe go against typical wisdom, startup wisdom.
zh: 那些可能与典型的创业智慧相悖的经验。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll tell you the biggest one.
zh: 我告诉你最大的一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, in the old days, which is three years ago, we would see a company, and if what they were doing, trying to do was too ambitious, we would, you know, not engage.
zh: 你知道,在过去,也就是三年前,我们看到一家公司,如果他们试图做的事情太过宏大,我们,你知道,就不会接洽。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just too crazy, too complex.
zh: 就是太疯狂、太复杂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, and implied by that is you wouldn't do $100 million seed because just it's too much money for almost any problem.
zh: 你知道,隐含的意思是,你不会做 1 亿美元的种子轮,因为对几乎所有问题来说这钱都太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too much money for any person to actually manage.
zh: 这笔钱多到任何人都没法实际管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too much money to build this sort of talent to absorb.
zh: 这笔钱多到组建起来的团队都吸收不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it doesn't make sense as an inception round.
zh: 比如,作为一个起步轮次这说不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think today we're almost seeing the opposite problem where, you know, an idea that's too small is not something that we want to engage with.
zh: 我认为今天我们几乎看到了相反的问题,你知道,一个太小的想法不是我们想要接洽的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can talk about how you put $100 billion to work in the seed productively.
zh: 而且你可以谈谈你如何在种子阶段把 1000 亿美元富有成效地投出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I'm not recommending you raise $100 billion, but I think that there's this sort of no ceiling on ambition is also showing up in how we're picking companies and maybe how they're picking us as well.
zh: 现在,我不是建议你募集 1000 亿美元,但我认为这种雄心没有上限的态度也体现在我们挑选公司的方式上,或许也体现在他们挑选我们的方式上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when we invest, we tell every founder, like, we're here to help you build the strongest form of your vision.
zh: 因为当我们投资时,我们会告诉每一位创始人,比如,我们在这里是要帮你构建你愿景的最强形态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Mark told this to me when him and I were talking about coming here and he said, Anish, the way we sort of told our story when we were raising our first fund was, you know, we were going to the moon or we were going to leave a moon sized crater in the ground and there was no other option.
zh: 你知道,Mark 在我和他谈论来这里的时候告诉我,他说,Anish,我们募集第一支基金时讲述我们故事的方式是,你知道,我们要么登上月球,要么就在地上留下一个月球大小的坑,没有其他选项。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's sort of how we want to work with our founders as well.
zh: 这基本上也是我们想与创始人合作的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that point.
zh: 我喜欢这个观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like is, can you get too ambitious?
zh: 那么就是说,有没有可能太有雄心了?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there like a limit?
zh: 有没有个限度?

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously you look at the, you know, the team and what they're, but kind of the key lesson here is be more ambitious.
zh: 显然你会看团队,看他们是什么样,但这里的关键经验是要更有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the opposite of what used to be of like, here's our, here's our wedge, here's where we're gonna go.
zh: 这和过去的想法正好相反,比如,这是我们的切入点,这是我们要走的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're looking for is just how big is the idea?
zh: 你要找的只是这个想法有多大?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, look at Adams.
zh: 我是说,看看 Adams。

speaker: Unknown
en: How crazy is Adams, you know?
zh: Adams 有多疯狂,你知道吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, what an incredible hero's journey for all of us collectively, but also what they're trying to do is something that, you know, five or seven or 10 years ago would have felt insurmountable.
zh: 我是说,这对我们所有人集体来说是一段多么不可思议的英雄之旅,而且他们试图做的事情,你知道,放在五年、七年或十年前会感觉是无法逾越的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's like, okay, it's challenging.
zh: 而现在就像,好吧,这有挑战性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see, you know?
zh: 让我们看看吧,你知道?

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else, anything else that has changed or I guess you've changed your mind about around what you think it takes to build a successful company these days?
zh: 还有什么别的吗,还有什么其他发生变化的东西,或者说在如今构建一家成功公司需要什么这个问题上你改变了想法?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I think that the kind of old wisdom around consumer products have to be free.
zh: 我是说,我觉得那种关于消费产品必须免费的旧智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm almost taking the opposite take, which is let's think about consumer products that are extraordinarily expensive.
zh: 我几乎在持相反的观点,那就是让我们想想那些极其昂贵的消费产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think every part of consumer discretionary spend is up for grabs right now.
zh: 我认为消费性支出的每一个部分现在都可以争夺。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a really useful, because price is a measure of product market fit, a really useful product exercise is what is the Birkin bag, 10,000 a month, 1,000 a month version of our product.
zh: 而我认为一个非常有用的——因为价格是产品市场契合度的度量——产品练习是:我们产品的爱马仕 Birkin 包版本、每月一万美元、每月一千美元的版本是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think expensive consumer software is something like new and important that we wouldn't have thought about five years ago.
zh: 所以我认为昂贵的消费软件是一种新的、重要的东西,是五年前我们不会想到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that framing because it just pushes you again to be more ambitious.
zh: 我喜欢这个框架,因为它再次推动你更有雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned Mark and you work closely with Mark Andreessen, Ben Horowitz.
zh: 你提到了 Mark,你和 Mark Andreessen、Ben Horowitz 紧密合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's one thing you've learned from each of those guys?
zh: 从他们每个人身上你学到的一件事是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: They're such extraordinary leaders, founders.
zh: 他们是如此非凡的领导者、创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the thing that I actually feel so grateful to be a part of that they really embody to their core, I think is a feeling of stewardship for the technology industry and for really the country and the sort of maybe the Western way of living and thinking.
zh: 我是说，我真正心怀感激能够参与其中的、他们发自内心真正体现的东西，我认为是一种对科技行业、对整个国家、甚至可以说是对西方生活方式和思维方式的责任感。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, and if you look at sort of a Ron Conway, you know, or Brooke Byers, Tom Perkins, there was this feeling, I think, of obligation to sort of leave it better than you found it from an industry perspective.
zh: 你知道，如果你看看像 Ron Conway,或者 Brooke Byers、Tom Perkins 这样的人，我认为有一种感觉，就是一种从行业角度让它比你来时更好的义务感。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that sort of aspiration goes way beyond just being the best investor in the world, though we want to do that too.
zh: 而这种追求远远超出了仅仅成为世界上最好的投资人，虽然我们也想做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see them both show up that way over and over again, where they want to do hard, important things that don't directly benefit the firm, or at least not singularly because they're just sort of important.
zh: 我看到他们两个人一次又一次地以这种方式出现，他们想做那些并不直接惠及公司的事情，或者至少不是仅仅因为重要才去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Ben has done a lot of that in the direction of the industry and Mark in sort of the direction of the country, though, of course, both work on both.
zh: 你知道，Ben 在行业方向上做了很多这样的事，而 Mark 在国家方向上，当然，两人也都在两方面都下功夫。

speaker: Unknown
en: Another really cool thing is just to see how I think Mark and Ben, but maybe the firm a little bit has shaped our collective ambition as a founder community.
zh: 另一件很酷的事情是,看看我认为 Mark 和 Ben,或者也许是这家公司一点一点地,如何塑造了我们作为创始人社区的集体抱负。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you look at five or seven or 10 years ago, deep tech was deeply unpopular.
zh: 我想，如果你看五年、七年或十年前，深科技是非常不受欢迎的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it wasn't a high status thing to be working on.
zh: 你知道，从事这个领域并不是什么高地位的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very fringe.
zh: 它非常边缘。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now it's become very popular, high status and mainstream.
zh: 而现在它变得非常流行、高地位且主流化了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's a lot of firms that have, of course, pulled in that direction.
zh: 当然，我认为有很多公司都在往这个方向发力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think that someone like Mark has been very full throated in his support of working on sort of capital I important work in the national interest.
zh: 但我认为像 Mark 这样的人，一直非常直率地支持从事那些大写 I 的、符合国家利益的重要工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And all of Silicon Valley has changed as a result.
zh: 而整个硅谷因此都改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you guys have had some big wins in the past couple of weeks, investing wise too.
zh: 而且你们在过去的几周里也有了一些投资方面的大胜利。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, thank you.
zh: 是的，谢谢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congrats.
zh: 恭喜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final question before we get to a very exciting lightning round.
zh: 在我们进入非常令人兴奋的闪电回合之前的最后一个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's your advice to product people who are trying to think about what they might want to shift in how they work, how they think, how they operate to be more successful in the future in their careers and with their companies?
zh: 对于那些正在思考自己想要在如何工作、如何思考、如何运作方面做出什么改变，以便在未来的职业生涯和他们的公司中更成功的产品人，你有什么建议？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just make more things.
zh: 就是做更多的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know it sounds silly.
zh: 我知道这听起来很傻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know everybody says it, but just please like come up with a project.
zh: 我知道每个人都在这么说，但请真的想出一个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to tell anyone about it.
zh: 你不必告诉任何人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be totally unimportant, but use it as a chassis to use all the new models, ship things, talk about them, build your own intuition.
zh: 它完全可以不重要，但把它作为一个载体，来使用所有的新模型、发布东西、谈论它们、建立你自己的直觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: I promise you're one sort of slightly frustrating and then very fulfilling week away from being as pilled as anyone.
zh: 我保证，你距离像任何人一样「上瘾」，只有一个稍微令人沮丧、然后非常充实的星期之遥。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you just got to use the technology.
zh: 所以你只需要去使用这个技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if not now, then when, right?
zh: 如果不是现在，那又是什么时候，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is all of us got in the game to build the products we saw in our mind's eye.
zh: 我们所有人都是为了让脑海中看到的产品成为现实才入场的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now you have a chance to do it.
zh: 而现在你有机会做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just please, please use the models, you know, and tell me what you built.
zh: 所以请，请一定去使用这些模型，你知道，然后告诉我你做了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Text me, you know, tag me, like I will reply and respond and engage with you and so will everyone else because we, the magic of Silicon Valley is that it's a very positive sum mindset, you know, it's sort of everybody is building on each other and vulnerability is really rewarded.
zh: 给我发短信，你知道吗，@我，我会回复、回应并与你互动，其他每个人也会，因为，硅谷的魔力在于它是一种非常正和的心态，你知道，每个人都在互相构建，而展示脆弱性真的会得到回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I definitely would encourage people to use the models.
zh: 所以我绝对会鼓励人们去使用这些模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's like a good heuristic if you're doing this enough?
zh: 如果你做得够多，有什么好的判断标准吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it like build something once a month?
zh: 是像每月做一次东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it like some number of hours per day sitting, talking, building?
zh: 还是像每天花若干小时坐下来、讨论、构建？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything that you think might help people be like, okay, you're doing a good job?
zh: 有什么你觉得可能帮助人们判断「好，你做得不错」的东西吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, just ship something once a week.
zh: 我是说，每周发布一次东西就行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it doesn't have to be crazy.
zh: 而且它不必很疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I mean, for example, when I was playing around with Codex, I had it build a slide deck for Mother's Day for my wife that pulled from my text messages.
zh: 你知道，我是说，举个例子，当我在玩 Codex 的时候，我让它为我妻子做了一份母亲节的幻灯片，它从我给他发过的短信里提取内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: It looked at my photo gallery.
zh: 它查看了我的照片库。

speaker: Unknown
en: It set some music to it, created like a 20, you know, slide deck of our relationship and pulled some cool old text from when I first asked her out.
zh: 它配了一些音乐，创建了一个大约 20 页的、关于我们关系的幻灯片，还找出了我第一次约她出去时的一些很棒的旧短信。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a really nice Mother's Day, you know?
zh: 那真是一个非常美好的母亲节，你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, it wasn't important.
zh: 我是说，它并不重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wasn't something that I might come back to, but it was shipping something.
zh: 它不是那种我可能会回头再用的东西，但那是发布了一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it can be that small.
zh: 所以它可以小到那个程度。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that our mutual friend, Nikhil Singal, you worked at Credit Karma with him.
zh: 我知道我们的共同朋友 Nikhil Singal,你和他在 Credit Karma 一起工作过。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had a really good way of thinking about this.
zh: 他有一个非常好的思考方式来看待这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: He finds that people flip on AI and how they feel about it once they find some moment of joy that it had created for them.
zh: 他发现，人们一旦发现了 AI 为他们创造的某个快乐时刻，他们对 AI 的态度就会翻转。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this Mother's Day idea is such a good example.
zh: 而这个母亲节的主意就是一个非常好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that's kind of a tip I always think about is just like, what's something that just will bring you joy if this works?
zh: 所以我认为那是我一直在想的一个小诀窍，就是，如果这个东西成功了，有什么是会给你带来快乐的？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's something you can do for someone else?
zh: 有什么是你可以为别人做的？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, maybe that's a good starting point as well.
zh: 你知道，也许这也是个不错的切入点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我很喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anish, before we get to our very exciting lightning round, is there anything else that you want to share?
zh: Anish,在我们进入非常精彩的快问快答之前，还有什么你想要分享的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything else you want to double down on before we get into the lightning round?
zh: 在进入快问快答之前，还有什么你想再强调一下的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think so.
zh: 我觉得没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've loved the conversation so far.
zh: 到目前为止我很喜欢这次对话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Me too.
zh: 我也是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round.
zh: 那么，我们进入了非常精彩的快问快答环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got five questions for you.
zh: 我有五个问题要问你。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you ready?
zh: 你准备好了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here we go.
zh: 开始了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are two or three books that you find yourself recommending most to other people?
zh: 有哪两三本书是你最常推荐给别人的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so, okay, Conquest and Cultures is my very favorite book.
zh: 好，嗯，《征服与文化》是我最喜欢的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's Thomas Sowell, and it just talks about how conquests have led to culture change in different societies around the world, sometimes positive, sometimes negative.
zh: 它是 Thomas Sowell 写的，讲的是征服如何在世界不同社会中引发文化变迁，有时是正面的，有时是负面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, to me, it's just the best historic view of sort of culture as the biggest driver of outcomes.
zh: 对我来说，它就是把文化视为结果最大驱动因素的最好的历史视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've experienced a lot of that as, you know, somebody who was born in Canada and moved here to America, which has a very different culture of ambition.
zh: 而且我自己经历了很多这种事，你知道，我出生在加拿大，后来搬到了美国，这里的雄心文化非常不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's that word again.
zh: 又出现那个词了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Conquest and Cultures is great.
zh: 所以《征服与文化》很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Seven Powers, you mentioned, is actually just an awesome book.
zh: 《七种力量》,你提到过，其实是一本很棒的书。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a very intellectual distillation about kind of, you know, moats and business theory and compounding advantages.
zh: 我认为它是对护城河、商业理论和复利优势的一种非常有智识的提炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: I really like it.
zh: 我真的很喜欢它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, maybe the third is the one that Mark, I actually thought that he was maybe punking me when he sent this to me.
zh: 你知道，第三本也许是 Mark 发给我的那本，我当时还以为他可能是在捉弄我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before I started, I said, Mark, are there any books that I should read?
zh: 在我入职之前，我问 Mark,有没有什么书我应该读？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he sent me a couple.
zh: 他给我发了几本。
